To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cyclosporine therapy increases total and low density lipoprotein cholesterol and triglycerides, decreases high density lipoprotein-cholesterol and apolipoproteins A-I and B, and increases total cholesterol/high density lipoprotein ratio.
cyclosporine therapy induces a reversible decrease in HDL and an increase in LDL and VLDL.
Cyclosporin and/or prednisone treatment induces an increase in plasma cholesterol and LDL cholesterol and a decrease in plasma HDL cholesterol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the effects of cyclosporing therapy in bone-marrow transplantation (BMT) patients.
the effect of cyclosporine on the lipid metabolism of bone marrow transplant patients.
the study of the effect of cyclosporine and prednisone treatment on lipid parameters of bone marrow transplantation patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cyclosporine treatment induces a reversible hyperlipidemia and a decrease of plasma HDL-cholestrol, whereas prednisone increases plasma total cholesterol mainly due to a higher increase in HDL cholesterol.
the addition of prednisolone to cyclosporing does not seem to be of advantage in terms of lipid metabolism.

cyclosporine treatment induces a reversible increase in LDL-cholesterolemia, and that the addition of prednisolone to cyclophosphamide and cyclosporine therapy does not prevent this effect, but rather increases it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the lipid profile of BMT patients treated with cyclosporine is altered in the direction of increased total cholesterol, LDL- cholesterol, triglycerides and VLDL-tri-glycerides and decreased HDL-cho-lesterol.
cyclosporine increases plasma cholesterol, LDL, VLDL, and triglycerides and decreases plasma HDL and apolipoproteins A and B.
cyclosporine treatment is associated with a decrease in high-density lipoprotein cholesterol and an increase in total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cyclosporine treatment increases plasma total cholesterol, LDL- cholesterol, triglycerides and apolipoproteins B and decreases HDL-cholestrol and apolipoprotiens A1.
cyclosporine therapy is associated with a decrease of the plasma HDL-cholestrol levels and an increase of the total cholesterol/HDL- cholesterol ratio.
patients undergoing allogeneic transplantation should be monitored for lipid changes and that the use of cyclosporine should be limited to the minimum required.
